Kenya crop field observations

12-county 2024–25 field observations Nakuru vs Nyandarua July 2024 crop-type map

12-county Kenya field observations (2024–25)

Source: all_kenya_25/kenya_county_data.geojson. County polygons: FAO GAUL 2025 (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). 6,114 GPS crop observations from 3,997 interviews across 12 counties, 79 sub-counties and 324 wards. Collected 13 Feb 2025 to 27 Apr 2025. This is not the July 2024 Nakuru/Nyandarua crop-type map — it is a later field campaign that records crop, planting system, season, condition, AEZ and calendar dates. Nyandarua is not in this file. Nakuru is in both.

What the file actually measures

Every row is one crop observation at a GPS point, not necessarily one farm. Shared kb_id prefixes group 3,997 interviews; 1.53 crop rows per interview on average, usually a maize–beans pair. Collection is entirely 2025 (Feb–Apr), but planting is 6,050 of 6,114 rows in 2024, and harvest is 5,428 in 2024 plus 686 in 2025. farming_ty here is water source (rainfed vs irrigated), not mixed/mono/agroforest. planting_m is Pure stand vs Intercropping.

How to read the geography

Coverage is western and Rift Kenya, not national: Bungoma is the largest sample (1121 rows), then Nakuru, Kisii, Narok, Trans Nzoia, Uasin Gishu and Kakamega. Kiambu, Baringo and Elgeyo-Marakwet are small samples. Polygons are FAO GAUL 2025 county boundaries. Grey polygons are neighbouring counties with no sample in this file. Colour is by sample counts, not cropland area.

Crops

Named crop_a is almost only maize and beans: 3,528 maize (63.6%) and 1,960 beans (35.3%) of 5,545 named rows. Potatoes (31), wheat (9) and everything else are rare as the primary crop. This campaign is a maize–bean system survey, not a full crop-type inventory.

569 rows have crop_a = No data

All of them are Intercropping. Kisii (289), Bungoma (156) and Kakamega (72) account for most. crop_b on those rows is Beans 365, Maize 194, Banana 3, Soybean 1. The crop was recorded as the companion, not as crop_a — do not treat Kisii as “no crop”.

Other crops beyond maize, beans, potatoes and wheat

They exist, but they are almost never the recorded primary crop. Of 6,114 rows, maize + beans + potatoes + wheat are 5,528 of named crop_a; only 17 rows have some other name in crop_a (tea, sunflower, finger millet, cabbage, cassava, banana, cowpeas, sorghum, plus 3 labelled “Other”). The rest of the diversity is hiding in crop_c — a third plant on an intercrop. Looking across crop_a, crop_b and crop_c together, 357 rows (5.8%) from 239 interviews mention at least one other crop. 96% of those rows are intercrops. Baringo has none.

Banana is the main “other” crop, and it is western

174 of 366 other-crop mentions are banana, almost all as crop_c: 88 in Bungoma (especially Kabuchai and Bumula) and 80 in Kisii (especially Nyaribari Masaba). Cassava (33) and cowpeas (25) follow, also concentrated in Bungoma. Coffee is 12 Kabuchai (Bungoma) rows as crop_c plus one Kiambu row. Tea is a handful of rows in Bomet East, Kuresoi South and Bobasi. Narok, Trans Nzoia and Uasin Gishu are maize systems with almost no other crops in this file.

Condition and agro-ecological zone

Condition is a five-level field rating. It is not yield. Western lower-midland counties (Bungoma, Kakamega, Baringo) have the weakest ratings; Bomet, Kiambu, Uasin Gishu and Trans Nzoia rate better. 14 irrigated rows are too few to interpret.

Data quality to watch

  • Sampling unit. 6,114 rows ≠ 6,114 farms. Use 3,997 interviews when comparing effort across counties. Narok has more interviews than Bungoma even though Bungoma has more crop rows, because Bungoma is more often a maize–beans pair.
  • Missing crop_a. 569 intercrop rows (9.3%), especially Kisii. Recover the crop from crop_b before computing richness.
  • Impossible calendars. 158 rows have harvest before planting. Median duration is still usable (beans ~14 weeks, maize ~27 weeks).
  • Altitude 0. 7 rows. Four AEZ values are missing.
  • Place names. 44 rows in Unknown sub-county (Trans Nzoia). Sub-county “805 Mogotio” was cleaned to Mogotio.
  • Not a diversity census. Only 13 named crop_a values, two of them dominant. Rare crops in crop_c (banana, cassava, coffee) are under-counted if you only use crop_a.
  • Overlap with the July 2024 map. Nakuru appears in both files but they are different samples, different dates, and different fields. Do not merge row counts. Nyandarua is only in the July 2024 map.

Nakuru vs Nyandarua crop diversity

Field labels from July 2024 crop-type mapping. Nakuru: 307 GPS points inside the county. Nyandarua: 161 digitized field polygons. Shannon index uses canonical crop_a names. This page does not need the internet. Hover a sub-county or a field dot for its name and numbers.

Nakuru is more mixed and more diverse

Nakuru has 21 crop types versus 6 in Nyandarua, and a Shannon diversity of 1.61 versus 0.50. Maize is still the main crop in both, but it is 61% of Nakuru labels against 88% in Nyandarua. Mixed and agroforestry systems are almost absent in Nyandarua (1.2%) and account for 11.4% of Nakuru samples, concentrated in Kuresoi South, Kuresoi North, and Molo.
